reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows that W addition in a different refractory HEA (TiZrWMo) forms Mo-W-rich precipitates and achieves high dynamic strength, but it does not demonstrate enhanced strain hardening, delayed shear localization, or improved uniform deformability, nor does it involve the HfZrTiTa0.53 system or the proposed heat treatment.
premises: W addition to a refractory HEA can form nanoscale W-rich precipitates
Nanoscale W-rich precipitates enhance dynamic strain hardening via Orowan mechanisms
Enhanced strain hardening delays adiabatic shear localization
Delayed localization improves uniform deformability and fracture strain under dynamic loading
These effects are achievable in the HfZrTiTa0.53 system with ~10 at.% W and low-temperature annealing
